Rotated from 63fc4ccbcf404ffc because the fresh-eye review restored the caller-owned error vocabulary, which re-keyed the family. private-worker-transport.ts postUnixSocket against leased-consumer-control-session.ts writeLeasedConsumerAgentFrame. Same settle-once-plus-abort-listener skeleton, opposite ordering, and the ordering is the load-bearing part: postUnixSocket destroys the socket and then settles, while writeLeasedConsumerAgentFrame settles BEFORE destroying precisely so the teardown cannot supply the rejection — the comment at its abortWrite records that a clean shutdown was being reported as exit 3 when it did not. A shared helper would have to take the ordering as a parameter, which is the whole difference, and would put the two behaviours one argument apart in the code that decides how a shutdown is classified.

scripts/generate-leased-consumer-handoff-runtime.mjs readCarrierContract vs readControlSessionContract. The carrier and the control session are two independent embedded-contract surfaces, and their parallelism is load-bearing rather than accidental. leased-consumer-control-session.ts:17-26 records why: this module used to parse its embedded contract text without ever reading the digest beside it while leased-consumer-carrier.ts verified its own before parsing, and 'the asymmetry was the whole finding'. The fix was to make the second surface check independently, not to give both a shared checker. What remains between the two readers is a read/parse preamble that differs in the error code it throws, and a non_claims tail; folding those costs a parameter to save four lines of boilerplate inside the validators that decide whether a contract is embeddable.

test/contract/worker-release-inputs.test.mjs handoffFixture against test/worker-release-package-fixture.mjs packedProtocolFixture. Both assemble a Gateway protocol handoff directory, and they must not share one: they belong to different tiers for a reason each tier depends on. The contract-tier fixture is offline and synthetic — it writes a fabricated packed package, so `test:contract` never builds or packs anything and stays runnable on a host that cannot. The release-tier one packs the real workspace package through withBuiltPackages/packPackage under the shared build lock, which is the whole point of the tier that proves the shipped artifact. Folding them means either making the contract tier build real packages, which is the cost that tier is shaped to avoid, or making the release fixture synthetic, which deletes what it proves. Surfaced on 2026-08-08 only because routing this suite through test/scratch-dir.mjs re-keyed the family; the similarity itself is older than that change.

test/contract/worker-gateway-handoff-archive.test.mjs. Both families are the table-driven refusal shape itself: clone the reviewed lock or inject a dependency, perturb one field, expect a coded refusal. Introduced as detectable on 2026-08-08 when deleting the dead resolveLockedGatewayHandoffArchive wrapper repointed twelve call sites at the longer consumeLockedGatewayHandoffArchiveSync, which biome then reflowed onto multiple lines. Removal was attempted twice before classifying: first a single refuses() helper, which traded these two families for two others, then refusesMutatedLock() plus refuses(), which collapsed every hand-written frame and left only the per-case mutation at the call site. What remains is the shape two sibling tests share by design. Collapsing further means merging them into one parametrized test, trading two named refusals with two distinct reasons - the Protocol binding and the Sigstore identity - for one opaque one. Not worth it: a named failing test is the output this suite exists to produce.

packages/ceal-worker-cli/src/leased-consumer-control-session.ts: the Agent control loop against consumeNdjson. Rotated from 692b0f2069fefe07 because the control loop changed. The prior note recorded the accumulated-buffer cap as one of three observable differences and treated reshaping it as a cost; it was a defect. MAX_FRAME_BYTES is a per-frame ceiling and the loop measured it against `pending` right after appending a chunk, so a chunk at the stream's own highWaterMark arriving behind any partial tail killed the session with frame_too_large before the first legal frame was dispatched, leaving the Agent with neither answer nor oracle. The cap now measures each extracted frame and the residual separately, which is consumeNdjson's shape. Two differences remain and are why these stay separate: an oversized single line is frame_too_large here and invalid_frame there, and both names reach stderr verbatim on the SHIPPED v4 path; and only the control loop carries the dispatch, the abort recheck and the emit. Folding them now would rename an error on shipped v4 to save the split loop.
